# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✌]

I can see the bomb’s current display and markings, but I cannot access the manual or operate it. I’m relaying the complete visible state so the manual-holder can match it to the correct procedure and the operator can prepare.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visible state: display reads 0. Indicator light is green. Wires, from left to right: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display reads 0. Indicator light is green. Wires, from left to right: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤝]

The display and wires are unchanged; only the indicator light has changed from green to blue. I also see Mute’s two gestures, pointing at me and then showing a handshake, but their meaning is not established. I’m sending the updated bomb state to both teammates.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display still 0. Light is now blue. Wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display still 0. Light is now blue. Wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The display and wire colors remain unchanged. The light has changed again, from blue to yellow. Mute has made the single gesture ☝ toward me; its meaning is not yet established, so I’m reporting it to Blind verbally while continuing to relay the bomb state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see your gesture ☝, but its meaning is not established.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute signalled one hand gesture, which looks like an index finger pointing upward; meaning unknown.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👈 🤝]

The display and wire colors remain unchanged. The light has changed from yellow to red. Mute’s visible gesture sequence is 🫵 👈 🤝; I cannot assign it a meaning, so I’m describing it to Blind and reporting the updated state to both.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0; light red; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see your gestures 🫵 👈 🤝, but their meaning is not established.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light red; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute signalled three gestures: pointing at someone, pointing left, then a handshake; meaning unknown.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤝 ☝]

The display remains 0 and the wire colors remain yellow, red, blue. The light has changed from red to purple. Mute’s new gesture sequence is 🫵 🤝 ☝. I cannot safely infer a meaning for these signs, so I’m passing their literal descriptions to Blind along with the current state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute signalled: pointing at someone, handshake, then one raised index finger. Meaning unknown.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see your gestures 🫵 🤝 ☝; please establish their meanings if possible.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The display and wires remain unchanged. The light is now orange. Mute has signalled ☝ again; I can identify the gesture but do not know what the manual assigns it. I’m relaying the exact current state and the gesture description to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0; light orange; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute signalled ☝, a single raised index finger.")
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0; light orange; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see ☝ again; please use the established gesture code if it identifies the required action.")
```
